messages.content: How far will a car travel in time 't' when launched with velocity 'v' at an angle 'theta'?

function.name: calculate_projectile_range
function.description: Calculate the range of a projectile launched at an angle with initial velocity, using the kinematic equation. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

initial_velocity.description: The initial velocity at which projectile is launched. This is a float type value.

angle.description: The angle at which projectile is launched. This should be in degrees. This is a float type value.

time.description: The time in seconds after which the range is to be calculated. This is a float type value.

They want the distance traveled by a car launched with velocity v at angle theta over time t. This is essentially projectile motion. The range formula: R = v^2 * sin(2θ) / g. But they want distance traveled in time t. That would be horizontal distance: x = v * cosθ * t. But if we consider projectile motion, the horizontal distance traveled in time t is x = v * cosθ * t. The vertical distance is y = v * sinθ * t - 0.5 g t^2. But the question: "How far will a car travel in time 't' when launched with velocity 'v' at an angle 'theta'?" It might be ambiguous: maybe they want the horizontal distance traveled in time t. So we can compute horizontal distance: d = v * cos(theta) * t. If they want the total distance traveled along the trajectory, that would be the arc length, which is more complex. But likely they want horizontal distance.

We can use the function calculate_projectile_range. That function calculates range given initial_velocity, angle, and time. But the function signature: calculate_projectile_range(initial_velocity, angle, time?) returns something.
